The base image moves from LinuxServer's now-EOL KasmVNC packaging to their actively-maintained **Selkies** stack. Same JDownloader, same config, a smoother web desktop.

Just **force update** the container. Your `/config` (JD install, settings, link list) is untouched; the WebUI still lives on HTTPS port 3001.

## Changed
- **Base image → `baseimage-selkies` (Ubuntu 25.10 / resolute).** Selkies streams the desktop through a hybrid VNC/H.264 pipeline for a smoother, lower-bandwidth web desktop; it is actively maintained, unlike the frozen KasmVNC packaging (its web client was archived in 2025). Everything JDownloader-specific carries over unchanged — the dark theme, auto-install, the dialog agent and theme healer, the ports (3001 HTTPS / 3000 HTTP), clipboard, PUID/PGID and `/config`.
- **A cleaner startup log.** The brand banner prints directly above the ready message as the log's final block, and the ready status is a tidy two-line `✓ JDOWNLOADER IS READY` instead of the old `###`-walled box. The full desktop log (launcher, theme healer, dialog agent) stays visible on the new base.

## Fixed
- **No login prompt, guaranteed.** Selkies' server enables basic authentication out of the box with a well-known default password, and the base's web proxy would even turn an *empty* WebUI Password field into a login with an unusable empty password. Both are neutralised, so the WebUI opens straight through — set a real **WebUI Username + Password** if you want it protected, exactly as before.

## Under the hood
- The window rules (borderless kiosk main window, floating dialogs) now re-apply on every start — the new base resets the window-manager config each boot, so a once-at-build patch would have been wiped.
- JD's graceful-shutdown settings flush (hidden columns, layout, link list) is preserved and merged with the new base's desktop teardown.
- The browser-tab favicon/branding uses Selkies' single icon path instead of the old multi-path kclient overrides.
- The template's auth fields are now labelled **WebUI Username / Password** (same underlying variables as before).
